evidence.excerpt: Thick-walled PP optical mounting brackets (nominal wall thickness 8 mm) for automotive lighting assemblies require tight dimensional tolerances and are particularly susceptible to warpage driven by differential cooling between the cavity and core sides of the mould. This study investigates the relationship between the cooling rate asymmetry and final warpage for four mould configurations with varying cavity-to-core mould temperature ratios (ΔT = 0, 10, 20, 30 °C; cavity side always colder). Warpage was measured on 15 parts per condition using a structured-light scanner with 0.02 mm point accuracy. Differential cooling induced a systematic bowing, with warpage increasing from 0.12 mm at ΔT = 0 to 0.91 mm at ΔT = 30 °C. Thermomechanical simulations captured this trend with a maximum error of 0.11 mm. Through-thickness crystallinity measurements confirmed that the core-side crystallinity exceeded the cavity-side value by up to 6 percentage points at ΔT = 30 °C, directly contributing to differential shrinkage.
